Elmo receives IEC 62443-4-1 ML2 secure-development certification

TÜV SÜD certified the motion-control supplier’s development lifecycle, covering documented security processes and post-release vulnerability handling.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗7 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

Certification of the supplier’s process

Elmo Motion Control announced on October 7 that TÜV SÜD certified its secure product-development lifecycle to IEC 62443-4-1 Maturity Level 2. Elmo supplies servo drives, multi-axis controllers and motors for applications including robotics and AGVs. The certification provides evidence for supplier assessments involving components integrated into automated equipment.

From design to maintenance

The program includes threat modeling during design, mandatory peer code review and independent security testing before release. Formal vulnerability and patch processes continue after release, with communication to customers. ML2 recognizes documented, repeatable development practices carried out by trained and qualified personnel.

What the certification does not establish

This part of the standard evaluates development practices, not whether an entire robot installation is vulnerability-free. Machine builders must still assess networking, connected equipment and update procedures in their own systems. Elmo says the program supports preparation for European cybersecurity requirements; it does not certify every compliance obligation of a customer’s finished machine.
